slots.label: Paragraph 2
slots.default: Newcastle has a genuine digital and tech cluster alongside engineering and energy work connected to the Tyne. It is also the furthest of the areas we cover from our engineers, which we would rather address directly than gloss over.

slots.label: Heading 2
slots.default: Distance changes the honest answer on onsite work

slots.label: Paragraph 5
slots.default: Our engineers travel from London and Stevenage, so a same-day visit to Tyneside is a longer undertaking than one in the South East. In practice this makes remote resolution and good remote tooling more important, and it makes us more careful about specifying hardware that will not need hands on it.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: Engineering and design workloads are heavier than office ones

slots.label: Paragraph 8
slots.default: CAD and simulation work needs specification and storage that ordinary office procurement underestimates, and the files are large enough to change how backup is designed.

slots.label: Heading 4
slots.default: Resilience matters more when help is further away

slots.label: Paragraph 11
slots.default: Where a visit takes longer, spare capacity and a documented recovery path are worth more than they would be in a city with an engineer twenty minutes away. That is a design decision, not an upsell.

slots.label: Heading 5
slots.default: Marine, offshore and energy engineering data

slots.label: Paragraph 14
slots.default: Work connected to the Tyne brings survey, inspection and design datasets that are large, retained for long periods and often gathered somewhere with poor connectivity before being brought back. That makes staged transfer and disciplined archiving more relevant than day-to-day office bandwidth.

slots.label: Heading 6
slots.default: Contact-centre style operations depend on the call path

slots.label: Paragraph 17
slots.default: Where a business runs telephone-based teams, availability of the voice path and its underlying connection is the service. Monitoring that reports on the network but not on call quality will miss the fault the business actually experiences.

slots.label: Heading 7
slots.default: Working offshore or on site means designing for intermittent links

slots.label: Paragraph 20
slots.default: Staff on a vessel, a rig or a remote site are not continuously connected, and treating that as a fault to be fixed usually fails. The better assumption is that work happens offline and synchronises when a link is available, with conflict handling that does not silently discard someone’s changes. It also affects security choices, since a control that depends on reaching a server in real time will lock out the person who most needs access.

slots.label: Heading 8
slots.default: Large engineering files need version discipline, not just space

slots.label: Paragraph 23
slots.default: Design and modelling work produces large files that several people revise. The failure mode is rarely running out of storage; it is two people working from different copies, or a reference file moving so an assembly no longer resolves. Check-out behaviour, a clear structure for references, and backups that capture a coherent point in time across the whole set are what prevent a day of rework.
